theme: sky and the reckoning of time
title: Stars on the night watch

plan.english: Brother, are you awake? I am awake, and I am guarding the cattle. Why are you not sleeping? I am looking at the stars. How many stars are there in the sky? No one knows that. Ask the old men; they have seen many nights. I will ask them at dawn. Look, but do not fall asleep!

title: Seven nights to the full moon

title: A hundred winters

title: Where the sun goes at night

plan.english: Father, tell me: where does the sun go in the evening? It sinks under the earth. In the night it walks back toward the dawn. Who carries the sun? The old men say this. Swift horses draw the wheel of the sun. Have you seen those horses? I have not seen them. But in the morning I see the light.

title: When winter goes away

Then the spring will arrive. I long for the spring. I too long for it. What will you do in the spring, sister? I will spin wool, and I will sing.

theme: sky and the reckoning of time
title: Shade at midday

plan.english: The sun is hot; let us sit in the shade. Let us sit under the tree. Are you thirsty? I am thirsty; give me water. Drink. The days are long now. When the sun goes down, we will go home. Then in the evening we will drink mead.

title: Here before evening

plan.english: Grandmother, the snow has come! Shall we go out and play? Go, and clothe yourselves! Be here before evening. Why shall we be here? In winter the night comes quickly, and the wolves come forth. We will be here before evening!

theme: sky and the reckoning of time
title: What is a month?

plan.english: Wise woman, what is a month? A month is the path of the moon. The moon is born, it grows, and it vanishes. And what is a year? A year is a winter and a summer. Why did you ask? May I become wise! You will become wise, if you listen.

theme: sky and the reckoning of time
title: The seven brothers

plan.english: Shepherd, tell me a story of the stars. Hear, then. Seven brothers dwelt in a village. They went up to the sky and became stars. Now they look at us. Show them to me! Those seven stars yonder. I see them! I shall not forget them.

title: The sun has vanished

plan.english: Elder, the sun has vanished! Darkness covers the earth! Do not tremble, boy. I saw this when I was young. Did the sun come back then? It came back, and the people rejoiced. Let us worship Sky, the father. Let us worship him; may he give us the light!

title: A star fell

theme: sky and the reckoning of time
title: Older than I

plan.english: Old man, this tree is stout. How many winters has it stood? It is older than I. My grandfather's father set it in the earth. Then it has seen many kings. It has seen kings and battles, and it is still standing. May your sons sit in the shade of this tree. May it stand for a hundred winters!

title: More beautiful than the moon

plan.english: Look at the moon, dear one! She has risen above the trees. She is beautiful and white. You are more beautiful than the moon. You speak sweet words. But the night is cold. Will you warm me? I will warm you, and the moon will watch us. What shall we tell my mother? We will tell her: we were watching the moon.

theme: sky and the reckoning of time
title: Why winter is cold

plan.english: Grandfather, tell me: why is the winter cold? In winter the sun walks away from us. Its path is short. And in summer? In summer it comes near, and it warms the earth. Which of the two do you love? I love the summer; then the nights are short. I love the winter; then we sit by the fire and tell stories.

title: When the new moon is born

theme: sky and the reckoning of time
title: A calf of three nights

plan.english: Herdsman, when was this little calf born? It came forth at the new moon; it has lived three nights. Its mother is that white cow. The calf drinks milk. It drinks, and it grows. At harvest time it will be a strong bull. Then it will lead the herd! Do you want this calf? I want it! Then give me a sheep for it.

theme: sky and the reckoning of time
title: When the ice leaves the river

plan.english: Old woman, when shall we plough the field? Plough when the ice has gone from the river. After the winter three moons will come; then plough. How will I know the right day? When the birds sing at dawn, that is the day. I will listen to the birds. Listen, and do not lie abed in the morning!

title: Remember me when the year turns

title: Dawn after the watch

plan.english: Brother, the night has gone away. Dawn has come forth in the east! Let us praise her, the daughter of Sky. Bright Dawn, drive the darkness away! The sheep are whole; no wolf came. Then let us fall asleep; we guarded the herd through the night. Are you hungry? I am hungry; let us eat porridge.
